**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 20 is a genuinely customer-favourable indemnity that meets or beats our preferred position on every element:

| Requirement | Where satisfied |
|---|---|
| Vendor IP indemnity, incl. affiliates | 20.1 — extends to Customer, Affiliates, directors, officers, employees, agents |
| Vendor breach of law | 20.2 |
| Data breach caused by Vendor | 20.2 (unauthorized access/disclosure of Customer Data) |
| Gross negligence / wilful misconduct | 20.2 (plus fraud and bodily injury/property damage) |
| Standard procedure | 20.4 — notice, cooperation at indemnitor's expense, control of defence, material-prejudice standard, settlement consent |
| Customer indemnity stays narrow | 20.3 — unmodified Customer material + Customer's violation of law, with carve-outs for Vendor Technology/modification/combination/instructions |

Two points worth highlighting on why I did **not** push further:

- **The fallback's 3× super-cap is unnecessary.** Section 21.3 makes "its indemnification obligations" an Excluded Claim, so Vendor's indemnity falls outside both the 21.1 cap and the 21.2 consequential-damages waiver — effectively uncapped, which is stronger than the fallback would give us.
- **The 20.1 IP indemnity has no exclusions at all** — no customer-modification, combination, or specification carve-outs. Proposing our model language here would actually have *weakened* our position, and 20.5's procure/modify/replace/refund remedy is expressly "in addition to" the defence obligation rather than a sole remedy.

I also confirmed nothing elsewhere undercuts the clause: 19.4 states the warranty remedy "is not exclusive for... infringement... or indemnified claims," 19.5 bars any disclaimer from limiting an indemnity, a search for "sole and exclusive remedy" returned nothing, and Section 1 has no competing definition.

**One item flagged for the adjacent limitation-of-liability rule, not this one:** "Fees" is defined at 1.7/1.8 as *only* the USD 12,000 Implementation Fee, and the 21.1 cap base references just the first Order Form. That is an unusually thin cap base and likely warrants attention under the LIMIT rule — but it does not affect the indemnity, which escapes the cap as an Excluded Claim.
